question: Should OpenClaw publish signed standalone Android APKs outside Google Play, and if so should the supported channel be GitHub Releases, F-Droid, or another maintained path?
rationale: The code can already archive a third-party APK locally, but turning that into an official install surface changes signing custody, sideload security, release provenance, and support policy.

options.title: Approve a standalone APK channel
options.body: Publish a signed third-party APK through a maintainer-approved channel using the existing Android release/versioning/signing path plus checksums and public install docs.

options.title: Stay Google Play only
options.body: Document that non-Play installs are unsupported for now and close this request only after maintainers accept the non-GMS user tradeoff.

options.title: Defer until further hardening
options.body: Keep the tracker open but block implementation until release owners finish the desired APK provenance, permissions, and support model.

recommendation.title: Approve a standalone APK channel
recommendation.body: Publish a signed third-party APK through a maintainer-approved channel using the existing Android release/versioning/signing path plus checksums and public install docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the current assignee and has recent Android app/docs history, making him the best visible owner for the product-channel decision.
